verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to the Buddha:

verses.pali: Katamesānaṁ kho, bhante, dhammānaṁ nirodho ‘nirodho’ti vuccatī”ti?
verses.english: The cessation of what things does this refer to?”

verses.pali: “Rūpaṁ kho, ānanda, aniccaṁ saṅkhataṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ khayadhammaṁ vayadhammaṁ virāgadhammaṁ nirodhadhammaṁ.
verses.english: “Ānanda, form is impermanent, conditioned, dependently originated, liable to end, vanish, fade away, and cease.
Its cessation is what ‘cessation’ refers to.

verses.pali: Vedanā aniccā saṅkhatā paṭiccasamuppannā khayadhammā vayadhammā virāgadhammā nirodhadhammā.
saṅkhārā aniccā saṅkhatā paṭiccasamuppannā khayadhammā vayadhammā virāgadhammā nirodhadhammā.
Viññāṇaṁ aniccaṁ saṅkhataṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ khayadhammaṁ vayadhammaṁ virāgadhammaṁ nirodhadhammaṁ.
verses.english: Consciousness is impermanent, conditioned, dependently originated, liable to end, vanish, fade away, and cease.
Its cessation is what ‘cessation’ refers to.

verses.pali: Imesaṁ kho, ānanda, dhammānaṁ nirodho ‘nirodho’ti vuccatī”ti.
verses.english: When they speak of ‘cessation’, its the cessation of these things that this refers to.”
